analysis.title: Fast Comment US: Backwards to the future, looking through rearview mirror; October Fed monetary policy decision
key_insights: The Fed held its policy rate at 3.75-4.0 percent, as expected by the market, by Handelsbanken's forecast and by the economist consensus.
The decision was not unanimous. Two FOMC members dissented in favour of a hike, whereas September's decision was unanimous.

Fed chair Kevin Warsh's communication was read as unexpectedly dovish. The FOMC wants an 'accumulation of more information' before any policy change, and Warsh was uncommitted to the rate hike that FOMC colleagues have signalled as appropriate this year.
The market reaction was yield curve steepening (lower front end, higher long end) and a weaker dollar. Handelsbanken expects a string of FOMC members to try to walk back this move.
Handelsbanken compares the communication to the July FOMC meeting delivery, which it calls disastrous, and sees increased risk of a dovish policy mistake.
Handelsbanken argues that underlying inflation is set to resurge, based on leading indicators, after a period when many gauges showed progress toward the 2 percent target.

Handelsbanken criticizes Warsh for three things: appearing unaware of leading indicator signals, saying he does not know whether strong supply- and demand-driven US growth is contributing to inflation, and being too relaxed about inflation expectations, which many measures show are high and rising.
Handelsbanken keeps its call for a December rate hike and forecasts healthy GDP growth and a strengthening labour market.
Warsh said he is 'unable and unwilling' to call current financial conditions 'tight'. Handelsbanken agrees conditions are not tight and expects the FOMC majority to conclude it has more work to do.
Handelsbanken says financial conditions may improve again after the midterm elections, a common pattern, and if the US-Iran war moves closer to its end.

The Fed will reduce its number of policy meetings. From next autumn one scheduled FOMC meeting will be reserved for strategy and major economic issues review with no policy decision. A second such meeting is added in 2028, giving 7 policy meetings in 2027 and 6 in 2028.
In the US data watch, Q2 2026 GDP was strong and Q3 nowcasts signal further lift, with risk of upside surprise to Handelsbanken's September Global Macro Forecast.
Payrolls have picked up and unemployment is declining toward levels below the estimated equilibrium. Labour market slack is limited because population and labour force growth are low.

Inflation has picked up with fuel prices, cost pass-through is increasing, and leading indicators signal more in the pipeline. Inflation expectations remain higher than normal and show signs of rising further.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held rates unchanged as expected, so the hold itself was priced. The surprise was in the communication, which was read as dovish.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed funds target range, December 2026 FOMC
macro_indicators.interpretation: Handelsbanken expects a December hike on healthy GDP, a strengthening labour market and rising inflation. The market reaction to this meeting suggests it is not fully priced.
One meeting a year (two from 2028) will be reserved for strategy and economic review with no policy decision.

macro_indicators.reading: Strong in Q2 2026, with Q3 nowcasts signalling further lift
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports the case for further tightening. Handelsbanken sees risk of upside surprise to its own growth forecast.

risk_factors: Risk of a dovish policy mistake if the Fed does not tighten while inflation resurges.
Inflation expectations are high and rising, and the Fed may be too relaxed about their anchoring.
Q3 growth could surprise to the upside, adding to inflation pressure.
Fuel prices are feeding cost pass-through into inflation.
vol_and_positioning: Yield curve steepened after the decision, with lower front-end yields and higher long-end yields, which Handelsbanken describes as policy-mistake-tinted steepening.
The dollar weakened after the decision.
geopolitical: US-Iran war: Handelsbanken says financial conditions may improve if the war moves closer to its end.
US midterm elections: financial conditions may improve again after the elections, per Handelsbanken.

tension_points.bull_case: Handelsbanken (hawkish view) argues that healthy GDP, a strengthening labour market, rising inflation and high inflation expectations will lead Warsh and the FOMC majority to hike in December. Two members already dissented for a hike now.
tension_points.bear_case: Warsh signalled the FOMC wants an 'accumulation of more information' before any policy change and would not call financial conditions tight. That points to a slower path and the dovish policy-mistake risk Handelsbanken describes.

theme_stances.key_argument: Healthy GDP, a strengthening labour market and resurging inflation will show the FOMC it has more work to do.
theme_stances.evidence: We stick to our call for December rate hike

theme_stances.key_argument: Warsh focuses on backward-looking data and ignores leading indicators and rising inflation expectations.
theme_stances.evidence: Warsh is not looking out the windshield, but at the rearview mirror
